title: Escalate planner effort on each plan revision, up to max
summary: Retry of job 20261113-161230-49ph (dispatched, never verified, no findings): re-implement and keep its 9-file scope. When planning thrashes (critic revise or mechanical plan-rule failure), each re-call of the planner runs one EFFORT_LEVELS step higher, capped at max; the first call and the critic are unchanged. Audience: operators reading invocation records.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria assert recorded planner effort rising across revisions, not just that the helper exists.
New unit and run tests; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Docs and decision entry written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (EFFORT_LEVELS at line 337, effort_for at line 830, effort validation at line 672), crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (agent_spec at line 394, 11 callers across athena-core) and crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs (the planner loop and revision handling). No new record or data file is added, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are unaffected; the effort already appears in the invocation record, so tests measure it directly from recorded planner invocations.

Job 20261113-161230-49ph: it was never verified and recorded no findings, so there is nothing to fix. Its scope is kept in full: all 9 files it changed are listed as deliverables, and its out_of_scope items are carried over. The retry re-implements from the base.

Escalation is by number of planner calls already made in the run: the first call at the configured effort, each later call one level higher, capped at max. This covers critic revises and mechanical revisions.
Consumers: none found for config changes; athena.toml is not changed, and escalated_effort is a new pure helper.
Environment: none; the work is local code, docs and tests, with no CI, push or records access.

docs/spec.toml and docs/decision-links.toml are touched only if the repository's own checks require them, for example a spec entry for the new behavior. A decision-links entry is added only if the new decision amends an earlier one or a [[governs]] path is touched.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs shows the escalation helper returns the level steps above base from EFFORT_LEVELS, stays at max when capped, and keeps an unknown base unchanged; `cargo test -p athena-data` passes.

A test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs drives planning with a critic revise then an accept and asserts, from recorded planner invocations, that the first call ran at the configured effort and the second strictly higher, while the critic's effort is unchanged; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.

A test covers the mechanical-revision path: a plan that breaks the plan rules is re-planned at a higher effort (asserted from invocation records), and a plan that still fails stops the job as before; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.

crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs passes an escalated effort only on a re-call (revision is Some) and the first call uses effort_for(Role::Planner); the diff of agent_spec in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs adds an optional effort override and every other caller passes None.

docs/design/job-planning.md describes the escalation (when it applies, one step per revision, cap at max), and a new appended entry in docs/decisions.md records the decision with a Provenance bullet; no existing decisions.md entry or file under records/ is edited.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change; athena.toml, defaults.toml and .github/workflows are unchanged.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass on the final tree (Athena's recorded check output on that tree counts).

out_of_scope: Changing the planner or critic model family or the [models] settings in athena.toml
Changing max_rounds, planner_usd or critic_usd caps
Adding thrash detection for other loops (producer, verifier)
Editing existing entries of docs/decisions.md or anything under records/
departures: Slightly higher than the reference: the change touches the planning loop, agent_spec and its callers, and several tests and docs.
hard_reason: It changes the run pipeline: how the planner is invoked during plan revisions and the plan-rule retry path.
